sections.text: Admach Systems Limited, BSE SME code544669, ISIN INE0XLO01010, listed31December2025. sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text: The company designs, engineers, fabricates, assembles and commissions customized special-purpose machinery, including steel-bar processing/finishing systems, non-destructive testing equipment, handling systems and packaging applications. Buyers require a process-specific machine rather than a standard retail product. Design knowledge, component procurement, machining, assembly, inspection, dispatch and commissioning create distinct operating and cash milestones. FY2026 domestic product revenue₹65.1611 crore and exports₹3.7488 crore total₹68.9099 crore; prior exports₹6.7214 crore show that total growth did not mean export growth. Revenue policy generally recognizes goods when substantial risks/rewards pass on dispatch or handover to the transporter, net of indirect taxes. Management says undelivered machines remain inventory. After-sales support is useful but no material recurring subscription stream is demonstrated.

sections.title: Moat, Customer Power and Competition
sections.text: Customized engineering and qualification can raise switching costs for an individual installed machine, and repeat industrial relationships support a moderate moat. They do not eliminate bidding, execution or customer-capex risk. IPO disclosures show top-ten customers supplied95.03% of FY2025 revenue,97.70% inFY2024 and98.60% inFY2023; the largest customer moved from63.06% to41.61% to19.44%. June2025’s short period again had83.33% from one customer. Such variation reflects project concentration rather than stable diversification. The prospectus says customers provide no long-term commitments. Top-ten suppliers represented54.52% of FY2025 purchases, while the broader supplier pool was312. Technical differentiation deserves credit, but monopoly pricing, proprietary licensing royalties and durable recurring economics are not established.

sections.title: Revenue Growth and Accessible Runway
sections.text: Restated revenue grew₹13.1048 crore inFY2023 to₹19.6824 crore inFY2024 and₹53.3582 crore inFY2025, then annual-report revenue₹68.9099 crore inFY2026. Three-year CAGR73.89% is real arithmetic from a small/lumpy base; the latest year’s29.15% is more restrained. OriginalFY2022 revenue₹14.5536 crore implies47.51% four-year CAGR, but original/restated scope differences are retained. October15 book₹76.25 crore includes GST; the new₹7.918 crore order also includes GST and has26-week execution,20% advance against guarantee,70% inspection payment and10% commissioning retention. September30 book₹69.04 crore is an earlier aggregate, not an additional order. Management’s MayFY2027 sales above₹100 crore, potential₹200 crore facility revenue and quotation pipeline above₹200 crore are aspirations/quotes, not contracted net sales or proven cash economics.

sections.title: Growth Quality and Incremental Capital Returns
sections.text: Core operating NOPAT, excluding all other income and using25% tax, is₹8.9801 crore inFY2026. A three-year accounting proxy compares₹0.6446 crore in restatedFY2023 with invested capital rising₹10.6997 crore to₹65.9133 crore:15.10% incremental return. Invested capital is equity plus debt less true cash, retaining CWIP, capital advances and margin deposits. This is around an assumed13–17% nominal small-company cost-of-capital range, not demonstrably above it. The FY2025–26 proxy is only about4.98%, partly because IPO-financed machines/CWIP have not fully contributed. Margin expansion on old operations is not a new-machine project IRR. CAP5 reflects mixed cohorts and unproven maturation, not a mechanical penalty for every rupee of CWIP. Persistent cash absorption warrants the Growth Quality cap even though sales and accounting earnings grew.

sections.title: Management, Governance and Capital Allocation
sections.text: Four Longani family promoters control the company. The annual report highlights52.95% post-IPO ownership, but its March financial-note named holdings sum about51.96%, and the prior-year Ajay holding differs between two tables. These presentation differences require a dated primary shareholding reconciliation; neither the undated input nor secondary percentages prove current ownership or pledge clearance. Director remuneration₹0.3614 crore is modest relative to PAT; disclosed reimbursements and salary balances are not evidence of diversion. The IPO identified delayed/missing ROC filings, DPT-3 mismatches, omitted RPT disclosures, missing signatures/attachments and historical director-remuneration noncompliance. Corrective filing/additional-fee statements do not erase the history. Older land-title transfer issues were explained in the restatement; FY2026 says deeds are in the company’s name, without independent registration verification here. CFO Shivdas Shinde resigned16May for stated personal/preoccupation reasons; Aniruddha Deshmukh was appointed21May, so no continuing vacancy is inferred. The audit is unmodified; audit-trail wording confirms a software feature, not an express full-year tamper-free test. IPO litigation summary had a₹1.32 lakh tax proceeding and no listed criminal case as of that document, not universal current clearance.

sections.title: Financial History, Cash Conversion and Forensic Findings
sections.text:
FY2026 revenue₹68.9099 crore, PBT₹12.0471 crore and PAT₹10.0128 crore compare with annualFY2025₹53.3582/8.3205/6.3025. RestatedFY2025 PAT is₹6.0981 crore, not the same vintage. FY2026 other income₹0.9304 crore includes₹0.6447 crore FX gain,₹0.215 crore export incentives and₹0.0707 crore interest. Effective tax16.88% is below the prior24.25%; management attributes the reduction to tax depreciation, without a complete quantified reconciliation. Removing all other income and taxing25–30%, or retaining export incentives at25%, gives normalized PAT₹7.78–8.50 crore. No wholesale add-back of advertising, write-offs or gratuity is made.
FY2026 CFO−₹4.5289 crore includes receivable absorption₹12.9472 crore, supplier settlement₹8.5873 crore and inventory absorption₹0.9187 crore, partly offset by other-current-liability funding₹6.2259 crore. Capex₹18.7985 crore and debt repayment₹10.6576 crore were funded largely by the IPO. Cash ended₹4.5215 crore; margin/FD₹1.1704 crore sits outside that cash and is not freely spendable. Inventory₹28.2443 crore includes₹18.9195 crore WIP. Receivables₹31.3215 crore include₹4.1276 crore aged6–12months and₹1.7784 crore aged1–2years. The comparative aging table totals only₹4.8308 crore against the prior balance₹18.3744 crore, a disclosure mismatch requiring correction.
OriginalFY2023 cash flow visually prints a₹5.1467 crore increase although opening/closing cash fall₹0.0095 crore. Later comparatives and the IPO restatement replace it with negative CFO. Original positive CFO is therefore excluded from quality claims. IPO-restatedFY2023/24/25 CFO is−₹2.2219/−7.9851/+0.4533 crore. FY2025’s subsequent annual comparative CFO₹1.5676 crore differs from the original₹0.5676 crore because₹1 crore FD redemption moved from investing to operating classification; total cash change is unchanged. These distinctions are not silent repairs or accusations of fictitious sales. Latest-three-year mixed-vintage CFO remains deeply negative under either classification, so CASH1 is robust.

sections.title: Valuation, Linked Scenarios and Funding
sections.text:
₹520 on19October is a dated secondary close, not an executable bid. With6772800 shares, market value₹352.1856 crore implies35.17x reportedPAT and41.44–45.26x normalizedPAT. Weighted historicalEPS₹18.39 must not be used with the post-IPO share count; current-count reportedEPS is about₹14.78. Zero March debt is positive but does not make inventory, advances or restricted deposits free cash.
The model starts from actual March balances: core operating WC₹45.2627 crore, cash₹4.5215 crore, debtzero, fixed assets/CWIP/capital advances₹22.5407 crore. It does not add IPO proceeds again or apply forecast WC ratios backward. Customer advances₹9.74 crore are management’s dated call disclosure; remaining current liabilities₹1.0989 crore plus tax₹1.7615 crore are conservatively settled once. Completion capex₹0–5 crore is a sensitivity, not a verified unpaid invoice. The IPO₹16.4743 crore machinery plan cannot be paid a second time after March’s₹18.7985 crore capex; exact object-to-asset completion remains unbridged.
Base growth30/25/20/15/12%,20% EBITDA margin,60% incremental WC and15x terminal NOPAT gives terminal₹583.81 and illustrative2.34% annual price return, but a₹2.07 crore reserve shortfall makes it unfunded without a changed plan. Bull45/30/25/20/15%,23% margin,40% incremental WC and18x NOPAT is funded and yields₹1086.55/15.88%. Bear−30/0/3/5/5%,12% margin,90-day extra collection delay,10% AR and15% inventory recovery losses produces₹19.40 crore funding need and an unfunded₹45.95 terminal illustration. No rescue debt/equity or dividends is assumed. Residual-capex/WC sensitivities are supplied. Base15% hurdle entry₹290.26 is only mechanical discounting of an unfunded case, not a buy price. R remains NS until funding/commitments can be supported.

sections.title: Bear Case and Capital Impairment
sections.text: Loss or deferral of one large project can simultaneously reduce sales, strand bespoke WIP and delay receivables. The October contract’s advance and inspection milestones mitigate exposure but require bank guarantees and leave commissioning retention; they do not establish cash terms for every old order. March zero borrowings improves solvency but cash₹4.52 crore is small against operating balances and remaining project needs. The severe model explicitly assumes collection delay and asset-recovery loss; it is not an observed default. Working-capital discipline, not physical floor space alone, constrains the₹200 crore ambition. D2 reflects the large funded-capital-at-risk and stress gap, balanced against no March financial debt and positive underlying operating earnings.

sections.title: Fivefold and Tenfold Outcome Tests
sections.text: Fivefold/tenfold current market value requires₹1760.93/3521.86 crore equity value before dilution. At an illustrative20x sustainablePAT, required profit is₹88.05/176.09 crore. At12% net margin this requires roughly₹733.72/1467.44 crore sales, versusFY2026₹68.91 crore and management’s unproven₹200 crore facility potential. Those figures exclude additional capacity, working capital and funding dilution. The modeled bull is only2.09x entry over five years. A fivefold or tenfold outcome is not impossible over a longer horizon, but neither its probability nor necessary capital economics is established.

sections.title: Monitoring Triggers and Falsification
sections.text: Obtain reviewed H1FY2027 P&L, balance sheet and cash flow rather than extrapolating order announcements. Reconcile receivable collections and the comparative aging table, tax-depreciation explanation, post-IPO ownership/pledges, capex invoices/CWIP commissioning and object-wise unspent proceeds. Verify which late-arriving machines were commissioned and whether cost savings actually offset depreciation and cash needs. Track net-of-GST executable orders, cancellations, advance guarantees and commissioning retentions. Cash-conversion improvement must survive supplier payments and exclude FD releases. Refresh dated BSE restrictions, lot, band and executable depth before any implementation. Further unexplained cash-flow changes, persistently aged balances or funding-dependent growth would weaken the case; sustained collections and attractive returns on the full invested capital would improve it.

sections.title: Classification and Completion Status
sections.text: Completed evidence-led deep assessment with explicit unresolved valuation/implementation constraints: conditional industrial-growth watchlist, not buy-ready, not a verified high-quality compounder. BQS4.76 and Growth Quality5.00 can be compared as bounded quality judgments; IAS is NS and cannot be ranked. G2 is conditional rather than an automatic failure solely for an older statement later replaced by disclosed restatements. Research completion does not mean all diligence gaps are solved or the company passes every gate.

Public document mirrors carry issuer-signed filings; secondary historical OHLCV is separately labeled. All60 trading datesJuly24–October19 appear after the verifiedDecember2025 listing.
